A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian simulations, nonlinear latent-variable experiments, and MNIST-SVHN-Text evaluations, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds a two-modality Gaussian experiment. Its separately attributed baseline scores do not replace these original contributions.

M1.justification: The masking objective, SumPooling and SelfAttention encoders, private-latent extensions, mixture models, and STL training algorithms remain unchanged. Much of the expanded method presentation comes from v1's appendices; the revised likelihood guarantee changes the analysis rather than the procedure.

E1.justification: V2 Section 5.1 adds a two-modality Gaussian scenario with strongly unequal modality-specific variation. The five-modality Gaussian simulations, nonlinear auxiliary-label and missing-modality settings, and MNIST-SVHN-Text coverage remain. Fully observed nonlinear results in v2 Table 4 already appeared in v1 Table 8.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the reported benchmark comparisons with externally sourced MVAE, MMVAE, MoPoE, and MMJSD scores in Tables 6–8 and 13. MVTCAE scores without the Text modality also appear in Tables 6 and 13. These supplement the retained controlled aggregation comparisons; they are attributed results, not documented new baseline runs.

E3.justification: The added Gaussian experiment specifies three latent variables and two scalar modalities with unequal private loadings. V2 also drops bound-gap and lower-bound metrics from the corresponding simulation tables. Reported architectures, training budgets, data sizes, and importance-sampling settings for retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 Appendix M's posterior-approximation diagnostics, linear rate-distortion plots, and linear beta-sensitivity analysis in Figures 3–5 disappear, along with Table 5's invariant-encoder evaluation on sparse ground-truth decoders. V2 adds an imbalance analysis with PoE numerical instability in Table 1. The MNIST-SVHN-Text sensitivity analyses and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: V1 Tables 2 and 8 explicitly report means and standard deviations over four repetitions; their merged counterpart, v2 Table 4, retains the values but omits that description. V2 also adds a five-dataset statement for the auxiliary-label study while Table 3 still specifies four repetitions, without explaining their relationship or establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds the Gaussian imbalance results and externally reported baseline entries, while removing v1 Table 5 and simulation bound-gap/lower-bound entries. For example, new Table 1 reports SumPooling LLH gaps of 3.6e-5 and 0.06 for the proposed and mixture objectives. Matched retained likelihoods, MCCs, coherence scores, classification scores, and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 Proposition 2 and Corollary 10 assert a general joint-distribution identity and likelihood lower bound. V2 replaces this with Corollaries 2 and 19, including additional posterior-KL and potentially positive encoder-mismatch terms, and states consistency conditions for a genuine lower bound. Appendix B also expands the mathematical analysis of Neural Process objectives. The identifiability proposition is retained and relocated.

C1.justification: The abstract changes from tightly lower bounding the likelihood to tightly approximating it. The contributions now distinguish a genuine marginal lower bound from an approximate conditional term. This materially narrows the central guarantee, while retaining the claims about flexible aggregation and benefits for identifiable models.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations involving empirical Bayes and VampPriors, context-dependent attention pooling, and finite-capacity Neural Process objectives. Remark 18 adds limitations concerning data supported on low-dimensional manifolds. Table 7 also explains that differing decoder-variance assumptions likely contribute to the large likelihood differences against external baselines.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix O adds iVAE and CPM-Nets code pointers for the existing data-generation and missingness procedures, alongside retained implementation references. Architecture tables, training schedules, and hardware disclosures largely match v1. The explicit description of constructing Text from English digit names at varying positions is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around empirical Bayes, VampPriors, manifold limitations, importance sampling, and diffusion-based multimodal or stochastic-process models. It adds an analytical comparison with the already cited MMVAE+ and relates its mixture extension to concurrent Palumbo et al. (2024). These are substantive additions beyond the reference-style conversion.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively reorganized and expanded. Material from v1 Appendices F, H, and I moves into v2 Sections 3.2, 4.1, and 4.3; distribution matching moves prominently into Section 2.1, while total-correlation material moves to Appendix C. The appendix contents list disappears, and explanations and terminology are revised throughout.

P2.justification: V2 changes typography, front matter, running headers, and figure arrangements. It merges existing results into Tables 2 and 4, adds a new experiment table and external-baseline blocks, and removes the linear diagnostic figures. Figure 1 expands using existing appendix images, and conditional-generation examples move into the main text.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important overstatement in the central result: its likelihood-gap decomposition and explicit consistency conditions replace v1's general lower-bound guarantee. This substantially improves the scientific qualification of the contribution, supported by clearer applicability limitations and baseline-setting caveats. Removing useful linear diagnostics and some replication detail weakens the empirical documentation, but the correction to the central guarantee provides the decisive overall gain.
